name: Exception Detail / Stack Trace Returned to Client
attack_scenario: The leaked stack trace/SQL error exposes framework versions, absolute file paths, table and column names, and internal IPs; the attacker uses this to fingerprint the stack, refine SQLi payloads, and locate other endpoints, turning a handled error into reconnaissance.
negative_test_hint: submit id = "' OR 1=1 -- " to force a SQLException and assert the response returns a generic 500 message with no stack trace, SQL detail, or file paths

exemplar.explanation: The KISA Java secure-coding guide flags '오류 메시지를 통한 정보 노출' (CWE-209) as one of the most frequently fixed weaknesses: getMessage()/getStackTrace()/printStackTrace() rendered into the HTTP response or a JSP error page. Log the exception server-side and return a generic message instead, which keeps stack traces, framework versions, absolute paths, and schema details off the wire and out of the attacker's reconnaissance.
